Field.Description: Use Apple hardware video encoding (UniFi cameras and HomeKit Secure Video)

Field.Label: Uses the Mac's VideoToolbox encoder instead of software. Much lower CPU use, especially with several HKSV cameras. Applies to new streams; the HKSV prebuffer restarts with the bridge.

Field.Description: Doorbell presses keep HomeKit Secure Video recordings going

Field.Label: A recording continues for 30 seconds after a press even if no motion is detected (e.g. a visitor standing still).
While you're speaking, the doorbell's own audio is muted so you don't hear yourself back (like a walkie-talkie). The visitor's reply comes through as soon as you stop.

Optional. Leave blank to use the bundled ffmpeg (6.x). Point at a newer build (e.g. /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg) to use it for all cameras; it's checked on save and the bundled one is used if it won't run.

Field.tooltip: Enter Camera Snapshot Max Refresh
Field.Label: Camera Max Refresh Rate (secs):
This is the maximum image refresh time when requested by Home App in seconds. We can't speed up requests, but we can slow them down if needed. Defaults to 30 seconds.

Field.tooltip: Away from home HomeKit asks for a small, low bitrate stream. Stream 2 is often Direct-to-wire and ignores this, so a re-encoding BlueIris stream is used instead.
Field.Label: BlueIris Remote Viewing Stream:

At home (Wi-Fi) cameras use BlueIris Stream 2 at full quality. Away from home (mobile) the stream chosen here is used, sized and limited to what HomeKit asks for. It must be H.264 with 'Direct-to-wire' unticked (BlueIris Settings > Web server > Advanced > Encoding). It is checked when the plugin starts; if it does not resize, Stream 2 is used and a warning is logged. Restart the plugin after changing.
